_notes: game_state added locally, from a 4-player game played through the cabinet's streamer rather than
by hand -- nothing here was read off a display and typed back.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x000348B8 and 0x000348B9, player low
and ball high, the shape every Stern SAM game checked uses. The player byte completed 1->2->3
three times, once per ball; the ball byte once.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109F0, the only group of four evenly spaced values
that rose monotonically through the game. A different base again -- 0x021109E4 on 24, X-Men,
twd_156c and Avatar, 0x02110A0C on Star Trek, 0x02110A24 on LUCI, 0x02110A9C on twd_160h.
The DMD confirms this map's champion labels: after game over it cycled BATMOBILE HURRY-UP
Confirmed after the table exited: the map decodes that game as 2,108,050 / 2,064,720 /
1,217,240 / 1,793,870, exactly what the DMD showed, with player_count 4. All three champion
entries decode as the machine displays them -- 'K O' 10,000,000, 'M R' 25,000,000 and 'JLS'
75,000,000 -- so the labels this map already carried are right.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 453-frame recording of live memory spanning an
operator-menu session and two consecutive games, the first tilted on ball 1. The session also
adjustment indices 30 and 32 as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
0x000348EA is the status bitfield trn_174h, avr_200 and avs_170 keep at ball+0x31, in a variant
without bit 0x01 during play: 1 in attract, 18 (0x12) playing, 20 (0x14) for exactly the eight
samples between the tilt and the end of the tilted ball, during which player 1's score sat
frozen at 275,210. The same declaration as those games -- game_over mask 0x12 inverted, tilted
bit 0x04 -- decodes correctly in all 453 frames across both games.
credits at 0x0211100C, the seventh SAM game measured at that address: rose to 2 with the coins,
then fell once at each of the two game starts.
